claims: Cancer is a group of diseases characterized by uncontrolled cell growth caused by DNA alterations.
Cancer often forms tumors or spreads via the bloodstream or lymph system.
Cancer occurs when abnormal cells divide without control, invading nearby tissues.
Main types of cancer include carcinomas, sarcomas, and leukemia or lymphoma.
Carcinomas affect skin or tissue lining.
Sarcomas affect bone or connective tissue.
Leukemia or lymphoma affect blood or immune system.
Cancer results from gene alterations that are DNA changes.
Gene alterations can be inherited.
Gene alterations can be caused by environmental exposures such as tobacco, UV radiation, and certain infections.
Tobacco is the leading cause of cancer.
Cancer diagnosis involves physical exams.
Cancer diagnosis involves imaging tests including CT and MRI.
Cancer diagnosis involves laboratory tests such as blood tests, urine tests, or tumor marker tests.
Cancer treatment includes surgery to remove tumors.
Cancer treatment includes radiation therapy.
Chemotherapy uses drugs to kill cells.
Immunotherapy boosts the body's natural defenses.
Targeted therapies attack specific genetic changes.
CAR-T cell therapy is a personalized immunotherapy.
In 2022, there were roughly 20 million new cancer cases worldwide.
In 2022, there were 9.7 million cancer deaths worldwide.
Cancer cases are expected to reach 33 million per year by 2050.
Up to 50% of cancer deaths are preventable.
Cancer deaths are preventable primarily by avoiding tobacco, maintaining a healthy weight, and limiting alcohol.
